__comment: Every secret the sample needs lives here and nowhere else, so it loads only when ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT is Development. These values are public - they are in a public repository - so a copy of this file signs tokens anyone can forge. In a real deployment each comes from the environment or a secret store, never from a file.

LocalLogin.__comment_signing: Asymmetric, so GET /auth/.well-known/jwks.json publishes the public half and a gateway can validate these tokens without being handed the ability to mint them. Set LocalLogin:SigningKey instead for HS256, which is the default and needs no key management.

TwoFactor.__comment: Its own key, not LocalLogin:SigningKey. Lose it and every enrolled user has to enrol again - a TOTP secret cannot be re-derived.
